To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ParaScope editor provides a new approach to parallel program development that allows the user to interactively explore the trade-offs between performance and correctness in parallel programs.

(1) the ParaScope Editor can be used to develop parallel programs, (2) it can do so by providing a sophisticated set of analyses and transformations, (3) it can do this in an interactive manner, and (4) its performance and usability are acceptable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new kind of parallel programming tool that provides a powerful set of transformations to the knowledgeable user.
the design and implementation of a tool that assists the user in understanding and transforming programs.
the design, implementation, and application of a tool to assist in the construction and maintenance of parallel Fortran programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ParaScope Editor is an excellent tool for parallelizing scientific Fortran programs.
the ParaScope Editor is an excellent tool for the development of scientific Fortran programs that use the parallelism available in current and future computer systems.
the ParaScope Editor provides the user with a powerful set of tools for the development of parallel programs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to provide a user with a sophisticated analysis, and a set of editing and transformation tools, that can be incrementally updated in response to program changes.

the ParaScope Editor has been designed to be a tool to help the knowledgeable user develop scientific Fortran programs, and it has been built to be an extensible tool that can be easily adapted to other languages and to other kinds of analyses and transformations.
the ParaScope Editor provides the user with a rich set of analyses, and the ability to quickly and safely make program changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ParaScope Editor is an example of a successful implementation of the ideas behind the "program transformation" paradigm.
it is possible to incrementally update sophisticated analyses of Fortran programs, including dependence information, as programs evolve.

the ParaScope Editor can be implemented in such a way that the user's editing and transformation activities can be performed with minimal overhead, while still maintaining a high level of accuracy and completeness in the dependence information.
